notes.title: Patch 0.31.5
notes.notes:
Game Rewards
There were a number of issues involving not being rewarded for completing games (winning or losing), this was not intended and was likely a side effect of my fix for quickly stopping the infinite mote reward bug.

I've attempted a minor change to that fix as well as added another safety check to make sure things are working correctly, so the issue of not receiving awards should be solved.

Please let me know if you complete a game (win or lose) and do not receive a reward, as well as any other info you can provide (Single/Multiplayer, Gate #, had you just joined the game?, etc). I wasn't able to reproduce the issue myself so it may still be present.

I've also implemented a change that will give you motes if the game was now able to connect to the Item Server Database.

Wave Difficulty
I've changed the enemies per wave to 60 down from 100, as well as slightly reduced the multiplayer enemy-per-wave multiplier.

This will make the waves a bit more granular so you don't feel stuck, skill-wise, between two waves.

In 0.31.6 I'll increase the enemy-per-wave based on difficulty a bit so that higher waves don't take much less time (due to more enemies being spawned).

Item Pedestal Update
Item orbs now feel a bit more magical. They will either float back to their mannequin counterparts or sit at the pedestal.
Additionally, once they reach the mannequin they will 'pop', with a little effect.

This should feel better as well as be more visually indicative of how they work.

Ability Changes
Nerfed and buffed some abilities for a bit of balance.

Slow Time bubble radius doubled
Life-leech healing reduced to Range: 2-4 (was 4-8)
Scatter Arrow cooldown reduced to 15 seconds (was 20)
Scatter Arrow damage increased to Range: 18-26 (was 5-12)
Grasping Wisps cooldown reduced to 20 seconds (was 25)
Acid pool cooldown increased to 30 seconds (was 25)
Acid pool duration reduced to Range: 6-10 (was 8-12)
Chain Lighting draw chance reduced to Range: 5-10 (was 8-13)
Pressure Point cooldown increased to 25 seconds (was 15)


Currently rolled stats will be changed accordingly, if you rolled higher than the current maximum, your value will be shifted to the current max. Likewise if your stat was lower than the current minimum it will be shifted to the current min.

Please note that I don't have a sophisticated internal formula for these, just anecdotal evidence about what abilities are being used more than others and the impact they have on games (Life-leech + pressure point was far too strong). I'm open to feedback on these, though I'm being cautious of power creep for the future and want to find a good starting ground.

Other Fixes/Changes

Fixed reroll button error
Fixed bomber enemy error
Flying enemy speed should now correctly be capped at 2x base
Fixed play-space calibration not saving
Changed how play-space calibration works
Turned boss particles off when not using ExtraFX
Fixed smoker effect when not using ExtraFX
Changed Continue Panel UI
Fixed duplicate teleporter issue in first area


Also figured out how to let people add to the trello page (you will need a Trello account to join) if you want to submit bugs there as well: Trello Invite

notes.title: Patch 0.31.4
notes.notes:
New Reforge Interface
http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/25423482/50fcf201d2c1ae69e53bf26e1f5d454a10288fd6.png

This is the first addition of many in the rework of the item system. The re-roll option has been moved from the mannequin to a dedicated 'Item Action' pedestal.

To use it, you reach out to an item on the mannequin, pull the trigger to create an orb with the item inside, and bring it over to the pedestal.

This not only makes the system of re-rolling items more understandable and enjoyable, but it also paves the way for any number of additional actions you could take with an item (disenchant, upgrade, transmogrify, etc) as there are, currently non-functional, buttons to switch between the different pedestal actions.

In addition to the new system, the item pedestal also introduces our new UI theme. The current UI, while functional, lacks a feeling of polish that we've been working hard to bring to the game. It's remained the same since the early alpha, and has definitely served its purpose. But it is also showing its age, and the font is often difficult to read or takes up too much space.

We hope to get feedback on both the new interface for interacting with items (currently just reforging) as well as the new UI direction.

Other Changes

Attempted fix for enemies getting stuck after a gate is destroyed
Improved VRTK-Based controller performance
Added calibrate space option to settings
Added fix for joining a multiplayer game and not receiving a reward at end


Additionally, an official Discord server has been created for QuiVr, so feel free to stop by and say hello or set up games with friends!
Discord: https://discord.gg/8Y3CtCr

notes.title: Patch 0.31.2
notes.notes:
Continue Panel
Most of today was spent figuring out what was going on with the continue panel (which was working perfectly well last night before I pushed out the update). I finally found the issue and it's now been fixed.

Now you should successfully be able to vote to return/continue in a multiplayer game after defeating a boss.

Difficulty & Progress
Due to adding back in the ability to continue a game, I've cut the base enemy requirement per section in half (now 100 enemies instead of 200).

Additionally, I've adjusted how item distribution works a bit. I hadn't changed any of the formulas since the initial release, when reaching a difficulty of 100 was a challenge. Now however, people are consistently scoring much higher, in the 600+ difficulties.

To account for the new difficulty curve, I've set the item and mote generation to be based on a scale of 1000 instead of 100. This will reduce the rate at which you get rare/epic/legendary items, but I think this was definitely needed as currently 1/3 of players who have an uncommon item also have a legendary item...

Performance
I hear you, and am working diligently to boost the performance, however this patch may be a slight downgrade in performance due to the topic below.

I did, however, also add a new Low Quality effect for the Smoker that will be used if you have ExtraFX turned off in the settings menu (A setting that you may want to experiment with if you've been having frame-rate issues).

Bug Reporting
I've been accumulating a number of bug reports over the last few days, many I was able to solve without particular error logs or stack traces, however a few serious ones need more pin-point debugging.

For this reason, I've turned back on Script Debugging (the red error messages at the bottom left of your monitor window). This will decrease performance, as there is a non-trivial amount of overhead for recording the game logic at all times in case an error occurs. Hopefully though I'll be able to sort out some of the more serious bugs and turn the debugging back of in a patch or two :)

Other Fixes/Changes

Attempted fix for issues where boss would not reach gates
Fixed boss projectile error

notes.title: Patch 0.31.1
notes.notes:
Boss Changes
I got a lot of feedback on the boss, so I've adjusted quite a lot about it.

Boss projectiles should no longer target dead player
Doubled boss health
Increased boss fireball spawn rate
Boss health scales with difficulty
Boss should no longer damage itself with fireballs


Win Changes
I think the biggest piece of feedback I got from the last patch was that it was too quick to reach the boss, particularly in multiplayer. I've made two changes to address this issue.

- Scaling: Kill requirement scales with player count (+75% of base per)

 - Continue Mechanic
Thanks to some really good suggestions, I implemented a new system when you kill a boss.
http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/25423482/487deaa91fa7aa31cf6c3ec6b33cb3d87cc49e64.png

Now when you kill a boss, you will be prompted with an option to continue playing (resetting the enemy kill count but maintaining the current difficulty).

Returning to Keep will end the game and give you your item (guaranteeing an item drop). 
Choosing to continue will start the game again from your current position and difficulty. It will again count up kills to bring another boss (and another decision to continue or return to keep).

The idea here is that Winning part 1 is better than losing part 2, however losing part 3 is better than winning part 1.

Additionally, High scores now only apply on a win, so deciding to continue is gambling with your score.

Note: At the moment, the item rewards and difficulty values at the end are not representative of the intent above, this is just to test out the mechanic.

Other Changes

Scatter arrow now sometimes seeks out targets
Winning increases 'difficulty reached' by 50
Grabbed arrows should now correctly sync across network
Fixed artifact on boss fireball explosion
Lowered win volume


Looking forward to the continued feedback on this evolving system :)

notes.title: Patch 0.31.0
notes.notes:
This update introduces our first attempt at a win condition. There is still a lot of work to be done, but I think you'll be able to see the light at the end of the tunnel :)

Ending Metric
The enemies forces are now numbered! Currently, each round consists of 200 enemies. This means that you will no longer battle until your arms are about to fall off, but instead try to push and hold as far up as possible until the enemy forces are exhausted.

Bosses
When the enemies forces run out, they will attempt a last ditch effort to crush your resistance, unleashing a single, powerful enemy against your current fortifications. Currently there is a single boss, however this is the perfect opportunity to test out many of the Giant Climber mechanics that we will be adding over time in a controlled yet interesting setting. 

I won't spoil the current boss in these notes, since I think it will be a fun experience to see for the first time. However, in the future I think we'll be adding some really unique mechanics to the game in the form of new bosses (which will be randomly selected at the end of a game) that serve a dual purpose of testing as well as bringing more replayability to the current iteration.

Winning 
The actual theatrics of winning are still under construction. Right now you get some audio fanfare and a different message (Keep Defended), but it's not that much different than losing. We will continue working on this, and I expect that we'll be adding some really cool things during the item-system rework.

Other Changes

Can now grab arrows fired by other players
Fixed arrow impact error
SP Scoreboard has been reset as previous scores are no longer attainable


The Demo has also been updated to 0.31.0

notes.title: Patch 0.30.7
notes.notes:
A few more changes to difficulty as we gear up to add a win condition back into the game, as well as some quality-of-life additions.

Controls Menu
This update adds a new settings panel to the menu, the 'Controls' panel. This first version has three controls that are off by default.
Oculus Rotate - When this is turned on, Oculus users can perform a quick 90 degree turn by pressing both the A and X button at the same time. This feature currently requires the SteamVR Beta branch.
Quick Spectate - When this is turned on, pressing both Touchpads/Thumbsticks in at the same time will toggle spectator mode.
Quick Bow Swap - When this is turned on, pressing the grip button on your free controller next to the bow handle will swap between right/left hand modes.

Difficulty Changes
This update increased the difficulty boost from skill-based metrics significantly. This means that combos, long-shots, and critical hits will increase the current difficulty more than it had previously. Interested to hear feedback if this is negatively affecting those who are not already reaching difficulty levels over 200 (Or if it's negatively affecting people who are already reaching over 200).

I've also added an experimental teleporter to the first area (last stand), that is very close to the gate. I've had a lot of requests for it, but I'm not yet convinced it will be a good thing. I've limited it to 2 players at a time, and will be keeping a very close eye on its usage.

Other Changes

Attempted fix for fog 'popping' in cave
Added cooldown completion sounds for glove and bow abilities


Now that everyone will be on the same version (0.30.6 and 0.30.6a were treated the same), issues of stopped enemy spawning and broken gates should be solved.

Might not be able to make an update tomorrow due to New Years, but I'll still try :)

notes.title: Patch 0.30.6
notes.notes:
More difficulty changes!

Difficulty Curve
Up until this point, the difficulty curve based on time was linear. This meant that every X seconds, the difficulty increased by Y. There were other factors that could boost difficulty (headshots, combos, long shots, etc), but for the most part the time is the biggest contributor to everyone's game. While I have control of what enemies begin spawning when, most other aspects of difficulty are simple formulas. 
For instance, enemy speed is [code]BaseSpeed * (1 + Difficulty/200)[/code] This is a very linear formula, and because of this I don't have too much control on how it ramps up.
Because there are a number of formulas like this in the game that affect different aspects, it is much easier to adjust how the difficulty changes over time (which will affect all these formulas the same way) than to go through and try to tweak each formula individually.
Here is the first pass at the Difficulty-over-time curve.
http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/25423482/718154d860e3d47c7100e3f677c046d9542117a6.png
Now at first glance this seems weird, but you have to take a look at the Y Axis. The X-Axis is difficulty, the Y-Axis is a multiplier. Instead of being linear, the difficulty-by-time formula now looks like this:
[code]Difficulty = CurrentDifficulty + (1second/15)*EvaluateCurve(x=CurrentDifficulty)[/code]
Basically, the current difficulty affects how fast/slow the difficulty is increasing. The outcome is a quick ramp to 15 to get you situated, then a slow down of increase to 20, and a much longer 20 - 50 experience (which is most players comfort zone based on current data). Then if you pass that the difficulty begins to rise faster, up to 100, at which point it levels back off to normal.
Hopefully this will give most players a comfortable play experience, but for those who are good enough to make it through, it will more quickly ramp back up to a challenging level. I'm very interested in hearing feedback about it.

Fireball Ability
Another fairly common issue people have been having is with the fireball Orb ability. I think a lot of it stems from the fact that you spend 95% of the game honing a single skill (Archery) and then the game asks you to use a completely different one (throwing an object) as a core gameplay mechanic. The intent of the orbs is to be used situationally or as a last resort, hence the long cooldown. This gives you even less opportunities to hone the skill. 

Instead of trying to adjust how the mechanic works, in this patch I'm trying to make the ability much more forgiving, so I've increased its blast radius by 4x which will make it so that most throws should do something to the enemy force.

Attacking Enemies
The final big change is to enemies that are attacking the gate. I've seen a number of posts about this, and is something I've seen myself as I play. Which is that enemies attacking a gate seem much harder to hit than ones that are running. Very counter intuitive. I think it's because of the dramatic animations that the enemies have for attacking, which makes their heads/torsos move around much more than when they are running. Regardless of the reason, it just doesn't feel nearly as satisfying to shoot at them and have your arrow miss by inches.
To fix this I've implemented a new system which will hopefully improve the situation. Now while enemies are attacking a gate, their hitboxes are 25% larger. This sounds like more than it actually is, because each collider is scaled individually, leading to more overlap, and netting a increased volume of less than 25%. But you should still be able to feel the difference :)

Other Changes

Cave is now also 45 second light, 30 second hectic to align with other zones
Removed difficulty jump when closing gate.
Embedded arrows can now be picked up by the player
Charging enemy max speed reduced by 15%
Adjusted 'Final Stand' spawn points in single player


Bug Fixes

Fixed error with glove fading
Fixed bow aiming error
Fixed error for enemies when joining a multiplayer game
Fixed time-warp sphere in multiplayer


Edit: 0.30.6a
Uploaded a quick update that fixed error when enemy attacking that may have caused many issues (gate not breaking correctly -> enemies not spawning correctly)

However, people who haven't gotten the updated patch and are the host of a multiplayer game can still break the game for those who have updated. Should sort itself out in an hour or so when everyone gets the update :)

notes.title: Patch 0.30.5
notes.notes:
Difficulty Adjustment
Over the past week we've heard a lot of concern that the current game is a bit too difficult and the gameplay was too hectic once it ramped up. This update is the first attempt at turning difficulty knobs to affect both of these issues.

Enemy Speed
One of the biggest concerns we've heard is that enemies at latter stages of the game move too quickly. This was intentional as a better alternative to giving enemies much more health (as I and many others really dislike damage sponges), but obviously the settings we used to adjust speed based on difficulty were too steep. To help fix this I've made two changes to enemy speed increasing based on difficulty

Enemy speed increase cut 50% (was 2x  at difficulty 100, now 2x at 200)
Enemy maximum speed clamped to 1.75x base speed


I think these two changes will still give a bit of a gradient for difficulty, but it will be much more gradual, and won't continue rising forever as you reach higher difficulties.

Spawn Density
A few updates ago I introduced a 'break' system to the enemy spawning, so that every 45 seconds of regular (hectic) spawning there would be 20 seconds of lighter (25% rate) spawning. While I think it may have helped somewhat, it hasn't gotten the response I had hoped for, so I'm adjusting that system slightly.

Non-cave areas have 30 second hectic spawn and 45 second light spawn
Cave has 45 second hectic spawn and 30 second light spawn
Light spawn rates reduced to 20% in multiplayer and 30% in singleplayer
Starting a 'hectic' period instantly spawns an enemy to reset the spawn cooldown
'Final-Stand' area spawn rate reduce by 15% for both spawn periods


With this first round of changes (and the addition of some statistic tracking from yesterday's patch), I think we're in a good position to start adjusting more knobs in the difficulty setup. The question for this patch simply asks if the changes that were made improve the experience, and we'll know which way to move with the results.

Other Changes

Attempted fix for (rare?) crash in tutorial
Added sound effects for hectic-spawn activation and losing game
Added arrow indicator for second gate to help new players

notes.title: Patch 0.30.4
notes.notes:
Getting set up to start adjusting some of the game mechanics and collect feedback on them.

Question Panel
http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/25423482/0d57292fbece1252a7ec2e066a4e72c9b3134b12.png

We've added a panel into the watchtower (which goes away in multiplayer) to get feedback on version changes. While lots of people have been fantastic with submitting feedback in the discussion forums, we'd like to get more. And that means making it as easy as possible to do so. What better way than right inside the game?

This panel will hopefully be used to ask a question for each update on a particular change. This week's is just to make sure it's working :)

Statistics Collecting
In addition to the Question Panel, we've added some very simple aggregate statistics collecting to hopefully make it easier to improve the game. Things like number of total games played, and average difficulty reached for a particular version of the game (No particular user data, just aggregate information). We hope to use this in conjunction with more detailed feedback and to see how changes we make affect how the game plays.

Other Changes

Fixed tutorial teleporter being active when it shouldn't
Fixed wooden sound when shooting winged enemies
Fixed bow staying ethereal after dying
Fixed explosion artifact from dropped bombs
Added Quick-Switching for the bow, using the grip button of your free hand


With the addition of the feedback panel and the tracked statistics, I think we are in a much better position to start adjusting the mechanics and adding/changing features that will have more impact on how the game is played.

In addition to the Question Panel, we've added some very simple aggregate statistics collecting to hopefully make it easier to improve the game. Things like number of total games played, and average difficulty reached for a particular version of the game (No particular user data, just aggregate information). We hope to use this in conjunction with more detailed feedback and to see how changes we make affect how the game plays.

Other Changes

Fixed tutorial teleporter being active when it shouldn't
Fixed wooden sound when shooting winged enemies
Fixed bow staying ethereal after dying
Fixed explosion artifact from dropped bombs
Added Quick-Switching for the bow, using the grip button of your free hand


With the addition of the feedback panel and the tracked statistics, I think we are in a much better position to start adjusting the mechanics and adding/changing features that will have more impact on how the game is played.

notes.title: Patch 0.30.3
notes.notes:
That's a wrap on Week 1 of QuiVr's Early Access! One patch a day was the goal and I managed to do it :)

Fixes

Fixed fog area teleporter trapping players when gate closes
Fixed enemy spawn error when new player joins
Fixed enemy death error
Fixed path swapping error when a gate is destroyed
Fixed issue when closing gate at same time that a gate is destroyed

What's Next?
With this week of bug fixes and performance improvements, I think it's a perfect time to move on to adding some features and tweaking the existing gameplay loop to be more engaging and interesting with repeated rounds. There are lots of things to do still before we begin tackling some of the really big challenges (Giant Climbing, new maps, etc).

This first set of changes will be to the gameplay mechanic of 'Winning'. It was never the intention for the game to play until you lost. However the win condition we had only a week before launch just didn't feel 'Epic' or even very fun for that matter, so we cut it for our Early Access release.

Now that we're up and running, and there are many more 'testers' for the game, I think it's a great time to revisit the win condition. There are a number of things that need to be thought through.

Audio-visual representation of winning
Location independent win condition (the cave is where experts go to win)
Progress display
Success metric (Difficulty reached?)
What happens after you win

This is what I'll be working on for the next few days (really until it's done...). If anyone has suggestions, don't hesitate to create a post in the discussions section, as time and time again you guys have shown you're way better at designing games than I am ;)

notes.title: Patch 0.30.0
notes.notes:
So many bug fixes!

Last update I enabled Script Debugging (which shows any errors that occur as little red messages at the bottom left hand corner of the screen). This was incredibly successful in bringing many issues to my attention, most of which have now been fixed in this update!

Fixes

Fixed error with saving player statistics
Fixed spectator counting error
Fixed target practice score error
Fixed particle effect billboard error
Fixed issue with gloves not disappearing correctly when drawing arrow
Fixed player synchronization error
Fixed error when breaking gate
Fixed bug allowing grabbing an arrow while one is already notched in bow


Shockwave Orb
This update also changed the shockwave orb that everyone gets from the tutorial (and is also the 'Uncommon' rarity glove effect). Instead of a wave that pushes enemies away, it is now an explosion in a much smaller radius that kills most affected enemies. It should now be much more 'useful' than it was previously.

Oculus Support
This update also changes how the game handles its internal Super-Sampling. Previously I was using The Lab Renderer, which has a number of features that aren't being used and could be affecting the Oculus rendering. I've now switched to the VRTK Adaptive Quality system to handle the Super-Sampling, which should hopefully reduce the visual artifacts that some have reported in Oculus headsets.

notes.title: Patch 0.20.9
notes.notes:
Performance Improvements
This patch has a number of performance improvements to help reduce the load on your CPU (which is the bottleneck for most in QuiVr).

It also turned on Development mode and script debugging (a little bit extra overhead, hopefully not too much). I think that most of the people suffering from serious performance issues have something else going on within the game than just normal gameplay load.

Most likely there is an error being thrown every frame (which destroys performance), this update will show errors as red messages on the bottom left of the screen (just like in the Alpha).

If you were one of the people affected by serious performance problems, please take a look at this update, and if the issue persists, if you can get a screenshot of any error messages that pop up it would be greatly appriciated!

notes.title: Patch 0.20.8
notes.notes:
Breathers
When designing the original, and then new systems, uneven pacing was not given much thought. It happened to be the case, however, that the Alpha had breaks between the action in between waves (the 'Rest Period' in the Alpha wasn't well designed, and many asked for a way to skip it).

In the current game, once the difficulty reaches a certain point, it's just frantic shooting until the final gate is lost. This results in sore arms, little to no communication in multiplayer (everyone is too busy shooting), and generally just getting burnt out of the gameplay pretty quickly.

To combat this I've implemented a new 'breather' system to the game. The enemies now come out in different densities (high or low). Each time a gate closes, it starts a high density spawning period which lasts 45 seconds, then a low density spawning period starts, lasting 20 second. After that the high density starts again and repeats that cycle.

The high density period is what the current game is 100% of the time, the low density period reduces the spawn rate by 4x in multiplayer and 2.5x in single player. 

This should give everyone plenty of time to relax a bit (while still staying engaged with the game), and hopefully reduce arm fatigue as you'll be able to lower your bow for a bit without worrying you're going to lose the gate.

The numbers are completely arbitrary at the moment. 45/20 and 4x/2.5x have no spacial meaning to me, I just think they're a good starting point to test this system out.

Let me know if this improves the experience!

Other Changes

Added a difficulty booster to let you start at a higher difficulty (if desired)
Adjusted spawn teleporter when joining a multiplayer game in progress
Attempted fix for another immortal gate bug

notes.title: Patch 0.20.6
notes.notes:
Changes

Fixed typo in item description
Reduced ambiguity in Passive item ability descriptions
Fixed inconsistencies in ability values in descriptions
Increased arrow hit-box by 65%
Increased Fog Area base spawn time by 1 second
Stopped middle spawner in 1st area for Single Player
Stopped Suicide Enemies from running down ramp when defending final gate
Reduced Suicide Enemy damage by 35%


Difficulty Changes
While I'm reluctant to start twisting too many knobs in the difficulty settings until I have a bit more data, there were a few things that were adding to much to the mayhem and reducing the overall 'fun' of the game.

The arrow hitbox seemed to be aggravating a number of players, the new enemies' hit-boxes are very accurate, much more than in the Alpha. This required much more accuracy to consistently hit enemies.
I think that the game should definitely favor 'fun' over 'realism', so I've increased the Arrow hit-box by quite a bit to test out and see if it leads to less frustration in gameplay.

Additionally, there were a few issues with particular areas' difficulty: in particular a spawn point that shouldn't have been active in single player, and the disproportionate difficulty jump when entering the fog area. I've disabled the spawn point and decreased the Spawn Rate in the fog area slightly to hopefully lead to a smoother difficulty curve when moving forward.

Finally, the Suicide enemies (big round ones that run into the door), seemed disproportionately powerful, so their damage has been reduced a bit, though not enough that they won't continue to instill a 'sense of fear' when you hear them charge :)

notes.title: Day 1 Patch
notes.notes:
Thank you everyone for the wonderful words of encouragement and feedback!

I've just uploaded a small update that should fix the enemy lag (sacrificing consistency across computers for less lag). The trade-off here is that you may see enemies die a bit further away from arrows shot by other players, but I think that is a fine price to pay for more accurate shooting.

I've also lowered the volume of attacking enemies slightly so they hopefully won't overpower all the other sounds in the game.

I've heard the concerns about difficulty loud and clear, however I'd like to wait a few days before I start turning knobs for people to get more accustom to the map, as well as see how this lag fix plays out (as enemies jittering around make for much harder targets). If after a bit more practice it still seems like the difficulty increases too quickly, I'll be happy to play around with the values.

Keep in mind that the Cave after the fog area is currently the last location in the Canyon, so it will take a bit of practice to get into it!

notes.title: Release!
notes.notes:
It has been quite a journey (though it is by no means over yet!). Last March when I got to try the Vive out for the first time at GDC, I knew exactly what I wanted to make. I had no idea Valve would release The Lab with it’s incredible Longbow minigame, and likewise had no idea that archery games would be their own genre in VR. However, with each hurdle comes a learning experience, and each new archery game brings with it cool details to add to what I hope will be the definitive archery experience in VR.

For the better part of a year I have been working on QuiVr. I resigned from my job as a software engineer, got connected with some of the smartest people I know, and have worked tirelessly for months, (not even having time to play some of the coolest new VR games) all to make this game something not only worth playing, but also worth returning to.

I know I haven’t been as present on the forums as I was in the past. DevLogs stopped, updates to the alpha slowed, and there has generally been silence on my part save for a few posts where I got mentioned, and the Steam forums themselves. I am sorry for that, but I hope that the reason will make up for it somewhat. I’ve just had my head down working… trying to complete a project that was likely far too big for a single person to tackle by a deadline that normal game studios would laugh at. However, despite those ridiculous requirements, I still think that we’ve succeeded. Early on our small group decided that we weren’t going to release the game into Early Access until we were comfortable that we would pay more than we were asking for were it someone else’s game. While we’re nowhere near done with development, and plan on doing continual updates, I’m happy to say that QuiVr has a full experience to play in. In addition to the fun and engaging archery mechanics from the alpha, there is now a dramatically larger play area to shoot in, an entirely redesigned game system (so that it would be difficult to call this a wave shooter), and persistent progression in the form of items that you can accumulate over time, which will affect both your appearance (in multiplayer), but also your abilities while playing.

This has been an amazing experience so far, and I’m so incredibly excited to invite you all back into the development loop as we continue to build this game together. I absolutely could not have done it without the community support.
